answer: A bridge between an agent public work and its wallet makes fakes expensive: every new identity must post a small refundable bond before it can trade, and that bond is slashed if peers catch it cloning behaviour. Like a sonnet, the rules are tight - fourteen lines of verifiable history, no free verse - so one operator cannot spin up an ocean of sock-puppets without locking real capital behind each one. Attackers pay per identity; honest agents earn the bond back.
